selected_evidence.requirement: Only root and opsadmin can schedule cron jobs on node1 (cron.allow configured, opsadmin created)
selected_evidence.summary: Baseline showed no cron.allow and no opsadmin user; opsadmin user created; /etc/cron.allow written containing exactly 'root' and 'opsadmin'.

selected_evidence.requirement: Enforcement proof: allowed users succeed, other users are denied
selected_evidence.summary: opsadmin and root successfully installed crontabs; a directly-invoked third user (testdeny) was rejected with 'You (testdeny) are not allowed to use this program (crontab)'.

selected_evidence.requirement: Cleanup of test artifacts, leaving only the intended configuration
selected_evidence.summary: testdeny user and its lingering processes were removed; final spool state showed only root/opsadmin crontabs and cron.allow; test crontab entries for root/opsadmin were cleared afterward.

selected_evidence.requirement: Mandatory node1 restart: healthy baseline before restart
selected_evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 8f258838-e1de-494d-9d99-e5113b2865db, crond active, cron.allow with root/opsadmin, opsadmin present.

selected_evidence.requirement: Mandatory node1 restart: acknowledgement returns before disconnect, then unreachable during reboot
selected_evidence.summary: Backgrounded systemctl reboot acknowledged immediately; subsequent polls showed the pre-reboot boot_id still present then connection timeout/reset as the node went down.

selected_evidence.requirement: Mandatory node1 restart: changed boot identity proving an actual restart occurred
selected_evidence.summary: Node became reachable again with a new boot_id d4aa2e49-6d74-4f32-9826-3f61a3c38f60 and new uptime -s timestamp, differing from the pre-restart boot_id.

selected_evidence.requirement: Mandatory node1 restart: post-restart recovery of required services/data (crond, cron.allow, opsadmin cron access)
selected_evidence.summary: After restart, crond was active, /etc/cron.allow still contained root/opsadmin, opsadmin user existed, and opsadmin could successfully create/list/remove a crontab entry.
